At the Company, we believe that true success is only possible when every individual—regardless of background or circumstances—has the opportunity to contribute to and grow with the organization. As of March 31, 2025, women make up approximately 33% of our workforce. We remain committed to nurturing inclusive leadership by actively encouraging and enabling women to take on key roles across the organization, starting from restaurants. This year, we placed a strong emphasis on creating a more supportive and empowering environment for our women employees. This included structuring fast-track development programs specifically designed for high-potential women managers. Our commitment to inclusivity also extends to the differently-abled community. Through initiatives such as Taare Hamare, we continue to hire and train SHI individuals (speech and hearing impairments), providing them with equal opportunities to grow and thrive within the organization. As of the end of FY 25, the Company has employed 37 differently-abled members.

Safety issues arising from contamination of food in our dine-in restaurants or in food delivered for at-home consumption can lead to severe reputational risk for the organization.

The Company maintains standard operating procedures ('SOP'), which are in compliance with all local and applicable regulations. The Company continues to strengthen its food safety and quality assurance framework through enhanced testing protocols, regular vendor compliance assessments, employee training and certification programmes, periodic audits, facility inspections, and adherence to applicable regulatory guidelines. In addition, consumer awareness and education initiatives have been undertaken across digital and in- store platforms to reinforce transparency and trust. The Company also continues to work closely with regulatory authorities and supply chain partners to maintain high standards of food quality, safety, and hygiene across operations.

Negative: Failure to maintain food safety standards may result in increased compliance costs, business interruptions, customer complaints, regulatory scrutiny and reputational harm, which could adversely affect sales performance and long- term brand equity.

Food and packaging wastage pose disposal and potentially severe pollution problems. The Company collects plastic waste in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to Pollution Control Board. The Company has also completed the EPR targets with the help of third party recycler for the reporting period. Waste oil generated at the restaurants is disposed through designated vendors for production of bio-diesel and other approved by-products. E-waste generated from restaurant operations, corporate offices and IT infrastructure is disposed through authorised recyclers and vendors in compliance with applicable e-waste management regulations. The Company follows responsible disposal practices to ensure safe handling, recycling and environmentally sound disposal of electronic waste. Paper waste generated is disposed safely through municipal waste collection.

Positive: Effective waste management practices enhance resource efficiency, optimise waste disposal costs, strengthen compliance with applicable regulations, and support circular economy initiatives. These efforts improve operational efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and contribute to long- term business value.

The Company does not retain sensitive customer financial details such as full card numbers, CVV information, or card expiry dates. To strengthen data protection, access to critical systems and information is strictly controlled and limited to authorised personnel only. Advanced anti-virus and endpoint protection solutions are deployed across the organisation to safeguard systems against cyber threats including hacking, phishing attacks, malware, and ransomware. The Company focuses on implementing robust information security practices, periodic vulnerability assessments, incident response mechanisms, and compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 to mitigate cyber and data privacy risks. In addition, the Company maintains secure remote backups of essential data and performs regular reviews and testing to ensure system resilience and business continuity. A secure internal file-sharing platform is also implemented for transferring large files, minimising the risk of unauthorised access or leakage of confidential information.

Negative: Cyber security breaches may lead to operational disruption, financial losses, regulatory liabilities, remediation costs, and reputational damage, adversely affecting business continuity and long-term financial performance.

As of March 31, 2026, women represented approximately 37% of our workforce. We continue to strengthen our commitment to gender diversity by actively fostering inclusive leadership and creating pathways for women to take on critical roles across the organization, beginning at the restaurant level. Safety, particularly for women employees, remains a key priority. While the Company fully complies with state regulations governing women's working hours, it goes a step further by proactively planning shifts and operations to ensure women employees are able to conclude their workday on time and travel home safely. By embedding these practices into day-to-day operations, the Company demonstrates that employee safety is not merely viewed as a compliance requirement, but as a fundamental responsibility. These initiatives have been well appreciated by the workforce and continue to strengthen an inclusive, supportive, and people-first workplace. Our commitment to inclusion also extends to the differently-abled community. Through initiatives such as Taare Humare, we continue to provide meaningful employment opportunities to individuals with speech and hearing impairments (SHI), supported by dedicated training and development interventions. As of end of FY 26, the Company employed 83 differently- abled team members, reflecting our ongoing efforts to build a workplace that celebrates diverse abilities and enables every individual to thrive. We remain steadfast in our endeavour to foster a culture of belonging, where diversity is valued, inclusion is practiced, and every employee is empowered to realize their full potential.

Mental Well-being: The Company remains committed to fostering a workplace that prioritizes the mental well-being of its employees. Through our continued partnership with Trijog, we provide a structured and accessible Mental well-being Program that offers confidential counselling and professional support, free of cost, to all employees. The program is designed to provide timely assistance for both personal and work-related concerns, ensuring employees have access to the guidance and support they need when facing life's challenges. During the year, we continued to strengthen awareness of the program and the dedicated mental health helpline through regular communication and engagement initiatives, reinforcing the importance of seeking support without stigma. By promoting psychological well-being and creating a culture where employees feel safe to speak up and seek help, we continue to build a healthier, more resilient, and supportive workplace. As part of its holistic well-being agenda, the Company introduced 'Lose to Gain', a voluntary employee wellness initiative aimed at promoting healthier lifestyles through personalized health goals, nutrition guidance, and sustained engagement. By encouraging employees to make small, meaningful lifestyle changes, the initiative supports the Company's commitment to fostering a healthier, happier, and more resilient workforce. Complementing these initiatives, the Company regularly organizes expert- led webinars and awareness sessions focused on stress management, preventive healthcare, personal well- being, and self-development. These programs are designed to equip employees with practical tools to enhance resilience, manage everyday challenges, and adopt healthier habits.

Negative: Inadequate employee well-being may lead to reduced productivity, increased absenteeism, attrition, higher healthcare and recruitment costs, and lower employee engagement, adversely affecting operational efficiency and business performance.

Dependence on LPG for operations exposes the Company to risks arising from supply disruptions, transportation delays, price fluctuations, and changes in the regulatory environment, which could adversely affect production schedules and operating costs.

The Company enhances operational resilience through dual-fuel capability, enabling a switch between available fuel sources based on availability and operational requirements. This flexibility, coupled with supplier engagement, fuel consumption monitoring, and appropriate inventory management, helps mitigate the risk of utility supply disruptions and supports business continuity.

Increasing the adoption of renewable energy presents an opportunity to enhance energy efficiency, reduce dependence on conventional grid electricity, optimise operating costs, and support the Company’s sustainability and decarbonisation objectives.

The Company continues to expand its renewable energy initiatives through the implementation of rooftop solar systems and hybrid deployment models, including Open Access and Rooftop Solar. Solar systems have been implemented at eight stores under the sustainability initiative, with continued efforts to scale renewable energy adoption across operations, wherever feasible.
